This report on IPCC’s media, outreach and other communication activities covers the period since the Sixty-second Session of the IPCC (IPCC-62) held in Hangzhou, China from 24 - 28 February 2025.

During this reporting period, the communications, media and outreach work prioritised planning, preparations and delivery of IPCC overall media relations and outreach activities at the 62 nd Session of the IPCC (IPCC-62) held in Hangzhou, China in February and those on the margins of the Short-lived Climate Forcers (SCLF) First Lead Author meeting (LAM1) in Bilbao, Spain, in March.

In March and April, a comprehensive communications effort was run in support of mobilising nominations of experts worldwide to serve as authors of the three Working Group contributions to the Seventh Assessment Report, as well as in support of the global call for nominations of experts to serve as Co-Chairs and members of the Task Group on Data Support for Climate Change Assessments (TG-Data).

For both critically important calls, a comprehensive set of communications assets was translated into all six United Nations (UN) languages and released along with videos featuring members of the Executive Committee.
Both calls were sustained communications efforts and ran until the closing deadline on 17 April 2025.

Over May, June and July, the work also shifted towards planning and preparations and delivery of series of IPCC’s engagement and outreach in key international fora, namely at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Subsidiary Bodies (SB62) in Bonn in June 2025, at the Twentieth Ordinary Session of the African Ministerial Conference on the Environment (AMCEN20) conference in Nairobi from 14 to 18 July and at the Sixth Forum of Ministers and Environment Authorities of Asia Pacific from 26 to 29 August in Nadi, Fiji.

During this reporting period, the communications, media and outreach work also prioritised planning, preparations and delivery of IPCC overall media relations and outreach activities through a major outreach event in Africa on the margins of the IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Cities (SRCities) Second Lead Author meeting (LAM2) in Mombasa on 25 and 26 July and preparations for the 63 rd Session of the IPCC (IPCC-63) held in Lima, Peru in October and 30 th Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC (COP30) in November.
Throughout the reporting period, the Communications team at the Secretariat has been dealing with a steady flow of incoming media and public queries and interview requests.

Additionally, the team has been managing overall outreach engagements and has played a crucial role in identifying and supporting IPCC speakers at various events and conferences as well as supported the recording and postproduction of Chair’s video messages and addresses for a number of international conferences and meetings.
In addition to this Panel progress report, the Secretariat’s Communications and Outreach team also provided regular reports to the IPCC Bureau and monthly reports to the IPCC’s Executive Committee.
During March and April, media work also supported the global call for nominations of experts to serve as authors for AR7 and addressed related media queries.
Following media work on SB62 and AMCEN-20 in June and July, most of the media relations work in August focused on announcing and publishing the list of authors for AR7.
Subsequent queries ranged from questions about the composition of the selected authors, regional and gender balance, as well as about authors from individual countries.
Some inquiries also involved comparisons between past and current cycles.
There was a notable interest in the statistics relating to the U.S. authors selected for AR7 and previous cycles.

Additional media requests sought factual information to support climate explainers on topics such as tipping points and the 1.5°C threshold, inquiries related to tropical forests and climate-resilient buildings.

In preparation for IPCC-63, planning and coordination with the hosts of IPCC-63 intensified during early September (at the time of writing of this report) and the team opened coordination with the hosts regarding media arrangements for IPCC-63, opening ceremony and potential outreach, as well as preparatory work on setting up of dedicated IPCC-63 media pages, coordination of media release and preparations for global distribution of speeches, videos, visuals and B-roll footage to facilitate media reporting from IPCC-63.

Since IPCC-62, IPCC communications and outreach efforts have focused on a rich programme of high-impact outreach activities that advanced public engagement and supported the development of the Seventh Assessment Report (AR7).

Following the conclusion of the IPCC-62 in Hangzhou, China, the Co-Chairs of the three Working Groups and the Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories (TFI) presented the agreed outlines of their contributions to the Seventh Assessment Report as well as provided a briefing on the Special Report on Climate Change and Cities to an audience of students, experts, and media at the Zhejiang Meteorological Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Centre.

The event featured remarks by senior figures, including the Deputy Administrator of the Chinese Meteorological Administration, the Deputy Secretary-General of WMO, and the IPCC Secretary and Deputy Secretary.

In support of the LAM1 meeting for the Methodology Report on Short-lived Climate Forcers (SLCF), an outreach event was hosted at the Bizkaia Aretoa Centre, University of the Basque Country in Bilbao, Spain, on 27 March.
The Co-Chairs of the Taskforce on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories (TFI) presented the outline of the SLCF Report for the audience, including experts, students, and media.
Moderated by TFI Bureau Member Maria José Sánz.
The event also included briefings on the role of the IPCC from Coordinating Lead Author Sophie Szopa and the IPCC Head of Communications.
The IPCC had a high-profile public presence at the 62nd session of the Subsidiary Bodies (SB62) of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in Bonn from 16 to 26 June.

In addition to Chair’s and Bureau’s active role and contributions to several mandated and other events, including the Chair’s keynote address at the opening of the Seventeenth meeting of the Research Dialogue, Chair’s opening of the joint SBSTA Chair-IPCC event on adaptation during which the Working Group II Co-Chair Bart van den Hurk and the WGII Bureau members presented an extensive update on the WGII activities, the IPCC also delivered a side event titled “Informing Climate Action: The science & cross-cutting topics of IPCC’s Seventh Assessment Report” which covered a comprehensive overview of IPCC’s seventh assessment cycle and presentations by the three Working Groups, including a segment on cross-cutting topics.
The IPCC Secretary´s statement for the opening plenary of SBSTA 62 and SBI 62 was submitted in writing to the UNFCCC Secretariat.

This event also featured a segment on the engagement of youth and Early-Career scientists, as well as a panel discussion on inclusivity and diversity within the IPCC.
This was followed by a public lecture by the Chair at the University of Nairobi titled “Assessing Climate Change: Scientific Needs for Africa and Beyond” on 14 July.
The 45-minute lecture included an extensive Q&A.

A half-day event also included presentations on the scientific content of the three Working Group contributions to AR7, as well as methodology reports delivered by the African Vice-Chairs of the three Working Groups and the TFI.

The Pan-African Regional Outreach event in support of the IPCC process in Africa was organized on 25 and 26 July 2025 at the Technical University of Mombasa in Kenya, on the margins of the Second Lead Author Meeting for the Special Report on Cities and Climate Change.

In agreement and coordination with the Kenyan IPCC Focal Point, Patricia Nying'uro and the WGII Vice-Chair Cromwel Lukorito, the objective was to increase awareness of and opportunities to contribute to the IPCC processes in Africa throughout the seventh assessment cycle and beyond.

In total, over 120 participants attended the event, including policymakers, national focal points, representatives from science and research institutions, funding agencies, postgraduate students, early-career scientists and researchers interested in contributing to the IPCC processes, as well as scientific experts and academics from five African sub-regions.

The two-day programme included presentations and panels focused on IPCC processes, ways to engage with the IPCC, relevant IPCC findings for Africa and scientific content of the upcoming three Working Groups’ contributions to the Seventh Assessment Report.
A follow-up survey showed overwhelmingly positive feedback.
Overall, the event achieved its objectives and was appreciated for its professional organisation, inclusivity, and knowledge-sharing impact.

Participants particularly highlighted that they gained a clearer understanding of the IPCC processes (84%) and showed readiness to apply knowledge and maintain professional connections with newly established contacts and IPCC (over 80%).
Respondents recognised this outreach initiative as a catalyst for strengthening Africa’s engagement with the IPCC process, particularly in AR7 and future climate assessments.

During July and August, the work shifted also towards preparations and support to IPCC Vice-Chair Ladislaus Chang’a, who represented the IPCC at the Sixth Forum of Ministers and Environment Authorities of Asia Pacific from 26 to 29 August 2025, held in Fiji.
In coordination with the UNEP Asia-Pacific Office and the Vice-Chair, the IPCC Secretariat developed supporting documents and background materials.

During the Forum, the Vice-Chair delivered three keynote addresses on behalf of the IPCC, participated in two speaking engagements, held an informal discussion, and attended several bilateral meetings.

Regarding upcoming outreach activities, at the time of the writing of this progress report (early September) the team is preparations for IPCC engagement at the 9th Asia-Pacific Climate Change Adaptation Forum taking place from 29 September to 3 October 2025 in Bangkok, Thailand, the preparation for outreach options at the IPCC-63 in Lima, Peru and planning of IPCC public-facing engagements at the UNFCCC’s COP30 in Belem, Brazil.

Two issues of the quarterly newsletter have been issued since the previous progress report.
Issue 24 was released in April 2025 (covering the first quarter of 2025) and Issue 25 in August 2025 (covering IPCC activities in the second quarter of 2025).
The next issue covering July to September 2025 is scheduled for early October.
The IPCC Newsletter serves as an internal communication tool to update the Focal Points from governments and observer organizations on IPCC activities in between Sessions.
The IPCC was mentioned over 1,660 (1,666) times from 1 January to 31 August 2025, in the top-tier 100+ news sources, as monitored by Meltwater.
Comparatively, during the same period in 2024, IPCC was mentioned 1,689 times in the top-tier media.

From mid-January 2025 to the time of writing of this report (8 September 2025), the IPCC website recorded a slight increase in audiences with just over 2, 2 million users compared to about 2. million during the same period in 2024.

Of the 2,245,075 users in the current reporting period, 1,001,318 came through direct visits to the website, 859,579 from organic searches, 322,757 were from referral sites, and 31,946 were from organic social media links.

Since the last Progress Report to the Panel at its 62 nd Session, IPCC social media platforms have been consistently focused on raising awareness about the IPCC’s scientific findings, ongoing activities, and opportunities for public engagement.

During the reporting period content published across all IPCC-managed platforms gradually shifted from thematic posts on the findings of the Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) towards the activities and narrative of the Seventh Assessment Report (AR7), amplifying the calls for nominations of experts to serve as authors for the Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) and the call for the TG-Data experts, as well as institutional messaging around main IPCC events, including the First and Second Lead Author Meetings for SRCities and SLCF and coverage of key outreach events.
One of the main highlights during this period was the sustained effort to raise the global profile of the call for nominations of experts to serve as authors for the Seventh Assessment Report.
To support the call, tailored multimedia content, including videos with Bureau Members, was produced in all six official UN languages.
A series of regionally based webinars organized by Bureau Members to support the call for nominations was also amplified via IPCC social media accounts.
IPCC social media also covered IPCC’s participation at SB62 in Bonn, Germany, and AMCEN-20 in Nairobi, Kenya.

Multimedia posts were developed from key outreach events, including LAM-1 SLCF in Bilbao and the Pan-African event, which took place alongside the Second Lead Author Meeting for SRCities in Mombasa, Kenya.
IPCC performance on social media platforms remained strong, with steady growth in the number of followers.
By the end of August 2025, IPCC had over 1.456 million followers across five key platforms (X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram and Bluesky).
Key moments of engagement were reflected in “post impression” figures, which peaked at over a million in March 2025, during the height of the AR7 author nominations campaign.
Videos shared in April garnered over 29,000 views.
